Draw normally distributed data with a target intra-cluster correlation

Source: R/draw_icc.R
draw_normal_icc.Rd

Uses a two-component variance model: each observation's value is the sum of a cluster-level draw (between-cluster variance) and an individual-level draw (within-cluster variance). The ICC equals \(\sigma_b^2 / (\sigma_b^2 + \sigma_w^2)\).

Usage

draw_normal_icc(
  clusters,
  ICC = NULL,
  mean = 0,
  sd = NULL,
  sd_between = NULL,
  total_sd = NULL,
  N = NULL
)

Arguments

clusters

Vector of cluster IDs (factor, integer, or character).

ICC

Target intra-cluster correlation, in \([0, 1]\). The endpoints are the degenerate cases rather than errors: at 0 the cluster variable does no work, and at 1 every unit in a cluster takes the same value.

mean

Grand mean or per-cluster mean vector. Default 0. May be given per cluster or already expanded to one value per unit.

sd

Within-cluster standard deviation.

sd_between

Between-cluster standard deviation.

total_sd

Overall standard deviation, \(\sqrt{\sigma_b^2 + \sigma_w^2}\). This is a parameter of the distribution, not a rescaling of the draw, so the realised sd() varies from draw to draw as any other sample statistic does. With ICC, it gives \(\sigma_{between} = s\sqrt{ICC}\) and \(\sigma_{within} = s\sqrt{1 - ICC}\). fabricatr 1.x instead rescales the finished vector so that its sample standard deviation is exactly total_sd every time; see the package vignette for why this diverges.

N

Optional; must equal length(clusters) when provided.

Value

A double vector of the same length as clusters, in the order the clusters were given.

Details

Supply any two of ICC, sd (within-cluster), sd_between (between-cluster), and total_sd. The other two follow from \(\sigma_{total}^2 = \sigma_b^2 + \sigma_w^2\). Supplying ICC alone is shorthand for sd = 1.

Examples

clusters <- rep(1:10, each = 20)
y <- draw_normal_icc(clusters = clusters, ICC = 0.4)
summary(lm(y ~ factor(clusters)))$r.squared  # approx 0.4
#> [1] 0.3377665
